source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 2 May 1930, p. 11 ("Local elections in Ulster: nominations in Derry")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: only the Liberties division was threatened, and 'Yesterday, Mr. Webb withdrew his nomination on account of his health, and Mr. Miller was declared elected'; the News-Letter heads the report 'No Contests for Derry and Down County Councils' (Belfast News-Letter, 9 May 1930)

note: Triennial election of Londonderry County Council. Nominations were received at Londonderry on 1 May 1930 by T. B. Adams, returning officer. Only the Liberties division was threatened, where the retiring member W. G. Webb was opposed by Charles C. Millar; Webb withdrew on 8 May on account of his health and Millar was declared elected, so no division was contested and no poll was held (Belfast News-Letter, 2 and 9 May 1930). 29 May 1930 is the statutory election day, not a polling day. The paper prints no party labels. Filed on 1930-06-05, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Londonderry that year (provisional); previously filed under 1930-05-29 (verification 5 Nov 2026). no nomination; the retiring member was deemed re-elected Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
